source.reason: Text states the M1 composition was fabricated using vacuum arc melting with 4× remelting; this is the first step of the processing history that leads (via homogenization) to the M1-HQ condition.

processing_steps_notes.value: Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C (M1) ingot fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of the raw materials throughout the ingot. This precedes homogenization and yields the as-cast precursor of M1-HQ.

source.reason: Text: 'Homogenization of as-cast samples was carried out at 1100 °C for 2 h, followed by water quenching'; Table 1 maps 'Homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching)' to the M1-HQ nomenclature.

processing_steps_notes.value: Homogenization of the as-cast M1 sample at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this condition is designated M1-HQ in Table 1 and is the state of the present sample.

source.reason: The processing-schedule figure shows the M1-HQ (water-quenched/homogenized) micrograph inset with a 100 µm scale bar and describes it as having lath/needle-like martensitic contrast; this is the only microstructural information reported specifically for the M1-HQ state.

overall_structure.value: Water-quenched (homogenized) condition of the Si-free alloy M1 (M1-HQ); optical micrograph shows lath/needle-like martensitic contrast.

source.reason: The methods section states OM was used to obtain microstructural images and describes the 2 % Nital etching; the M1-HQ micrograph inset in the processing-schedule figure is an optical micrograph showing lath/needle-like martensitic contrast.

measurement_conditions.value: Sample prepared by standard metallographic grinding and coarse/fine polishing, then etched with 2 % Nital solution (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10–15 s

purpose.value: To obtain the microstructural image of the homogenized/water-quenched M1 (M1-HQ) sample

source.reason: Thermo-Calc (TCFE9) equilibrium calculations were performed to design the M1 alloy (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C) and predict its equilibrium phases/austenite fraction; these CALPHAD results pertain to the M1 alloy of which the present sample is the homogenized state.

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Systematic addition of Al to the Fe–8Mn-0.2C system; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; equilibrium phase fractions and austenite composition evaluated as a function of temperature, yielding a predicted ICT range of 600–900 °C and equilibrium austenite fraction of ~50 % at the selected IAT of 700 °C for M1.

unmapped_findings: M1-HQ is the homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching) condition of the Si-free alloy M1 (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C); the paper's detailed microstructural characterization (SEM/EBSD), XRD phase quantification and uniaxial tensile testing were carried out on the hot-rolled (M1-HR) and intercritically annealed (M1-IA) conditions rather than on M1-HQ, so no tensile, hardness or quantitative phase-fraction data are reported specifically for M1-HQ.

Per Table 1, the M1 (3Al-0Si) sample naming convention is M1-AC (as cast), M1-HQ (homogenized, 1100 °C/2 h + water quenching), M1-HR (hot rolled, ~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C) and M1-IA (intercritically annealed, 700 °C/1 h + water quenching); M1-HQ was an intermediate processing state shared by both steels (M1-HQ and M2-HQ).
